name: Bookwhen
shortDescription: A UK online booking system for events, classes and courses, with capacity management, passes, memberships, payments and attendee communication.
suitableContexts: Churches running regular groups, courses or bookable activities
Teams needing paid and free booking workflows

pricing.summary: Bookwhen has a free plan for small, free events and four paid tiers with volumes from 300 to 4,000 bookings per month. Its help centre directs buyers to the pricing page for current plan prices; online payments use Stripe or PayPal and their fees are separate.

tiers.label: Free
tiers.detail: Up to 50 booking spaces per month for small, free events; no paid tickets

tiers.label: Lite
tiers.detail: Up to 300 bookings per month; paid ticket costs are available

tiers.label: Standard
tiers.detail: Up to 800 bookings per month with passes, memberships and waitlist features

support: Live chat support Monday to Friday, 9am–5pm UK time on paid plans
Phone support stated for higher plans

editorial.assessment: Bookwhen is a credible UK choice where a church runs repeated bookable activity rather than occasional one-off ticketed events. Its free plan has clear limits and the paid tiers scale by booking volume, so a church should estimate transactions—not simply attendee numbers—before selecting a plan.
bestFor: Regular courses, groups and activities with capacity limits
Churches wanting passes, memberships or waitlists as booking volume grows
strengths: Free plan for small free events
Features designed for repeat activities and courses
limitations: Current paid subscription prices need checking on the supplier’s pricing page
Online payment fees are set by separate providers

longForm.verdict: Bookwhen is most compelling for a church with a rhythm of recurring activities: a course, a midweek group, children’s holiday activity or room-based session with capacity limits. It is less about maximising ticket revenue and more about giving staff a reliable routine for bookings, reminders and attendance.

decisionLens.heading: Count bookings, not just people.
decisionLens.text: Bookwhen’s tiers use booking volume. One family booking multiple places may not be the same as multiple transactions, so inspect a recent season of activity before choosing a tier. Also decide which bookings genuinely need online payment and which can remain free or offline.

sections.heading: From a one-off event to a recurring activity
sections.question: Is Bookwhen the right shape of tool?
paragraphs: Bookwhen’s published plan comparison includes tickets, capacity, reminders, attendance tracking, passes, memberships and waiting lists. That suits activities where the same process repeats and staff need a dependable view of availability.

The free plan is limited to small free events, while paid tickets and more advanced features begin on Lite or higher. Test the public booking page, cancellation approach and an actual register with the volunteers who will use it.

userFeedback.summary: This profile does not use an independent review score. It is based on Bookwhen’s official help information about plans, features, payment providers and support.
themes: The platform is organised around recurring bookings and capacity management.
Subscription tier and payment-provider cost are separate planning questions.
userFeedback.caveat: Bookwhen’s help centre advises checking its pricing page for current paid-plan prices. This directory does not infer them from older material.

faq.question: Does Bookwhen have a free plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Its help centre describes a free plan for small, free events with up to 50 booking spaces per month, with important feature limits.

faq.question: Can Bookwhen take payments?
faq.answer: Paid tickets are available from the Lite plan upwards. Online payments use Stripe or PayPal, whose transaction fees are separate from the Bookwhen subscription.

faq.question: Does Bookwhen have UK support?
faq.answer: Bookwhen says paid plans include live chat support Monday to Friday, 9am to 5pm UK time. Confirm the support level for the plan you are considering.
